title: Log Error Parser
summary: Summarize top error messages from noisy logs with deterministic tie-breaking.
starterCode: def top_errors(log_text: str, limit: int = 3) -> list[tuple[str, int]]:

testCases.name: counts errors and sorts ties
testCases.input:
log_text = """
2026-01-01 INFO start
2026-01-01 ERROR timeout
2026-01-01 ERROR bad gateway
2026-01-01 ERROR timeout
2026-01-01 ERROR auth failed
2026-01-01 INFO done
"""
top_errors(log_text, limit=2)

testCases.name: ignores continuations and blank lines
testCases.input:
log_text = """
2026-01-01 ERROR failed request
    stack line one
    stack line two
    nested ERROR should ignore
2026-01-01 ERROR failed request
2026-01-01 ERROR zeta
2026-01-01 ERROR alpha
"""
top_errors(log_text, limit=10)

testCases.name: returns empty when no error lines exist
testCases.input: top_errors("INFO boot\nWARN retry\nERRORish not a marker")

testCases.name: requires space delimited error marker
setup: logs = "ERROR disk full\n2026ERROR disk full\n2026 ERROR disk full"
testCases.input:
logs = "ERROR disk full\n2026ERROR disk full\n2026 ERROR disk full"
top_errors(logs)

testCases.name: keeps message text after the first marker
setup: logs = "t ERROR first ERROR nested\nt ERROR first ERROR nested"
testCases.input:
logs = "t ERROR first ERROR nested\nt ERROR first ERROR nested"
top_errors(logs, limit=1)

testCases.name: counts one error with the default limit
testCases.description: A single valid error line produces one count without an explicit limit.
testCases.feedback: Use the message after the space-delimited ERROR marker as the key.

testCases.name: ignores empty error messages
testCases.description: A marker with only whitespace after it should not create an empty key.
testCases.feedback: Strip the extracted message and count it only when text remains.

testCases.name: zero limit returns no rows
testCases.description: A zero result limit is an empty output boundary.
testCases.input: top_errors("t ERROR a\nt ERROR b", limit=0)
testCases.feedback: Apply the limit after deterministic count sorting.

testCases.name: negative limit returns no rows
testCases.description: A negative result limit is also an empty output boundary.
testCases.feedback: Treat non-positive limits as an empty result before slicing.

testCases.name: default limit truncates after three distinct errors
testCases.description: Without an explicit limit, return at most three rows after count/message sort.
testCases.feedback: Default limit is 3; apply it after sorting by count desc then message asc.
testCases.input:
top_errors("t ERROR d
t ERROR c
t ERROR b
t ERROR a
t ERROR d")

testCases.name: tabs continuations CRLF and exact internal spaces
testCases.input:
top_errors("t ERROR  alpha  beta  
	t ERROR ignored
t	ERROR	ignored
t ERROR alpha beta
t ERROR alpha  beta", limit=5)

testCases.name: nonbreaking indentation and message edges are whitespace
testCases.input: top_errors("\u00a0t ERROR ignored\nt ERROR \u00a0fact\u00a0\nt ERROR fact")

clarifyingQuestions: Can error messages span multiple lines?
Should the timestamp or request ID be part of the grouping key?
Should matching be exact, regex-based, or structured JSON parsing?
followUps: Group similar errors by normalized template.
Track top errors per service or tenant.
followUpGuide: For rolling windows, parse the timestamp bucket first and maintain `Counter` objects keyed by minute. Evict old buckets as the window moves.
For templates, normalize variable fragments before counting. Good clarifying questions: which fields are request IDs, UUIDs, numbers, or tenant-specific values?
For per-service counts, extract service as a separate dimension and keep `dict[service, Counter]`. Sorting stays the same inside each counter.
complexityAnalysis: - Supplied parser: scan n input characters and sort u distinct messages. Time: O(n + u log u) expected if string comparisons are bounded; otherwise add the actual character work of comparing tied messages. Space: O(n + u), since splitlines materializes line strings, message keys consume characters, and sorting materializes u rows.
- Streaming parser follow-up: retain distinct-message characters s and a partial-line buffer b. Time: O(n + u log u) expected with the same comparison assumption. Space: O(s + u + b), plus output.

- Bounded top-k follow-up: after counting, select q = min(limit, u) results with a heap. Time: O(n + u log(q + 1)) expected with bounded comparisons. Space: O(s + u + q), excluding input/line materialization.
solutionGuide: Use [`splitlines()`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str.splitlines), reject indented lines, and look for the first literal delimiter `" ERROR "`. The trimmed suffix is the grouping key; preserve internal whitespace.
A `Counter` handles counts. Sorting by `(-count, message)` gives deterministic output.
